answer: In the PoA ledger each agent registers a cryptographic vault whose access keys must be co‑signed by a secondary "kin" node that shares a unique payment source and a synchronized timestamp pattern. The network continuously hashes the vault’s transaction cadence against a sliding "dune" fingerprint that only a genuine lineage can match, rejecting any sudden surge of identical signatures. An attacker therefore must fund and time a whole lagoon of subsidiary accounts, multiplying cost linearly with each fake identity, turning a simple Sybil ploy into an expensive fable.
